jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

As a Senior Data Analyst on our Enterprise Systems team, you will turn K2 Space's operational data into the insights that drive smarter decisions across satellite design, manufacturing, and mission operations. You'll partner with engineering, production, and finance to understand what's working, what isn't, and what needs to change. Then build the reports, dashboards, and automation that make that visibility scalable. If you're energized by fast-moving environments and want your work to have a direct line to hardware getting to orbit, this role is for you.

Responsibilities

Develop automated reports, dashboards, and analyses that surface KPIs, performance drivers, and trends. In direct support of strategic or operational decisions.
Build and manage data pipelines integrating structured and unstructured data sources across K2's enterprise systems.
Design and implement automated workflows using SQL, Python, Snowflake, and related tools to standardize data, minimize manual error, and uphold data integrity and governance best practices.
Develop and maintain data retrieval processes and application integrations across multiple systems and data sources.
Partner with internal stakeholders across Manufacturing, Finance, Propulsion, Materials, and other disciplines to analyze drivers impacting production outputs and operational scaling.
Develop, maintain, and distribute recurring reports for Manufacturing, Finance, and Production teams, accurately and on schedule.
Support regulatory, financial, and accounting reporting by compiling and validating the underlying data.
Evaluate existing processes around data QC, and report distribution. Identify inefficiencies and deliver concrete improvements.
Own documentation for data tools, analyses, and workflows; keep it current and usable.
Stay current on advancements in data analytics, automation, AI/ML, and BI tooling.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related STEM discipline.
6+ years of experience in a data analyst or analytics role.
Proficiency in SQL and Python.
Working experience with Snowflake and a modern BI platform (PowerBI or Tableau).
Experience working with relational databases and building complex data visualizations.
Ability to translate ambiguous business questions into structured analyses and clear recommendations.
Comfortable modifying established workflows and troubleshooting data issues as they arise.

Nice to Have

Experience with ETL processes and workflow automation.
Background in manufacturing, finance, or operational data domains.
Strong knowledge of financial reporting processes.
Familiarity with physical manufacturing workflows.
Experience mentoring or informally leading analysts on a data team.

Compensation And Benefits

Base salary range for this role is $140,000 - $180,000 + equity in the company
Salary will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level
Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision/ coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks

If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, we encourage you to still apply! Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other and non-traditional career twists and turns are encouraged!

TCEQ employees get some great perks, including paid leave, health insurance, and state and federal holidays. See Benefits and Perks at TCEQ.

TCEQ Hydrologists support Texas Water Rights, Groundwater, Surface Water, and Water Supply programs. This role will collect hydrological data; analyze findings; and assist with data calculations and the development of recommendations for programs and/or projects to support effective water resource management and policy decisions.

NOTE: Please list all related software experience on your application. RiverWare experience is highly preferred.

HYDROLOGIST HIRING PROGRAM

This program aims to establish a pool of applicants suitable for filling TCEQ Hydrologist positions.

How does the Hydrologist Hiring Program work?

Hiring supervisors in the Austin Central Office, or any of TCEQ's sixteen regional offices, may request candidates with specific hydrology experience and geographic preferences from the Hydrologist Hiring pool. You may be connected to all open positions that match your experience. The hiring supervisor schedules interviews and makes a final selection.

TCEQ provides great career advancement opportunities with clear paths for professional growth and development.

Education & Experience

Hydrologist I

A bachelor's degree in hydrology, engineering, geology, mathematics, or natural or physical science from an accredited college or university.

Hydrologist II*

A bachelor's degree in hydrology, engineering, geology, mathematics, or natural or physical science from an accredited college or university, plus two years of full-time experience performing hydrologic work of similar character, scope, and complexity in the areas listed in examples of work performed.

Hydrologist III*

A bachelor's degree in hydrology, engineering, geology, mathematics, or natural or physical science from an accredited college or university, plus four years of full-time experience performing hydrologic work of similar character, scope, and complexity in the areas listed in examples of work performed.

Hydrologist IV*

A bachelor's degree in hydrology, engineering, geology, mathematics, or natural or physical science from an accredited college or university, plus six years of full-time experience performing hydrologic work of similar character, scope, and complexity in the areas listed in examples of work performed.

Hydrologist V*

A bachelor's degree in hydrology, engineering, geology, mathematics, or natural or physical science from an accredited college or university, plus eight years of full-time experience performing hydrologic work of similar character, scope, and complexity in the areas listed in examples of work performed.

A graduate degree in hydrology, engineering, geology, mathematics, or a natural or physical science from an accredited college or university may substitute for one year of the required experience, with a maximum of two years substitution allowed.

Accordingly, the ability to maintain the security or integrity of the infrastructure is a requirement to be hired for and to continue to be employed with TCEQ.

Applications remain on file for one year from the date of receipt. Eligible individuals may submit a new application for an additional one-year period.

Job Summary

This position is located in the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants (OVSJG), Victim Services Division. The mission of the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants is to develop, fund, and coordinate programs that improve public safety; enhance the administration of justice; and create systems of care for crime victims, youth, and their families in the District. OVSJG supports and coordinates the development and implementation of a comprehensive system of care for crime victims within the District of Columbia. OVSJG advocates on behalf of victims at all levels of government and community; and works to ensure that comprehensive services are available in the District for victims of crime. The ACP program allows eligible individuals to receive mail at a confidential address and provide a legal substitute address for the individual's physical address on public records. The incumbent is responsible for administering the District's Address Confidentiality Program (ACP), which involves planning, research, data collection, analysis and evaluation, and providing training to community members and advocates.

Duties And Responsibilities

Supports the coordination of the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) activities in order to develop program policies, procedures, forms, and other materials. Identifies and collects performance metrics for OVSJG to report on the ACP in order to evaluate and address concerns regarding the efficiency and operation of the program. Reviews and provide recommendations on ACP applications to the Program Manager and agency leadership in order to streamline participant enrollment into the program. Interprets and provides guidance to leadership and advocates; advises on unclear or vague policies and procedures relating to the ACP. Identifies problems and specific issues in a particular area of ACP and advises the supervisor of existing problems in order to recommend solutions or alternatives for program implementation and supporting survivors. Develops and provides training to community-based organizations that serve as ACP application assistants for clients in order to aid in their enrollment into the program. Provides guidance and technical assistance to District agencies in order to implement the statutory requirements of the program.

Maintains records of any certified or registered mail received on behalf of a participant. Maintains information and documentation regarding the ACP databases to track actions and provide periodic reporting, or projects that relate to the program. Receives first-class, certified, and registered mail sent to a participant at a substitute address in order to forward mail to respective participants. Represents the program at community events; meets with individuals, community-based organizations, DC government agencies, etc.; participates in related conferences, meetings, and training seminars in order to report findings and essential information back to senior staff. Coordinates project phases with technical and professional stakeholders involved in the project. Provides information, as required by project specifications in order to communicate information and decisions concerning projects with all interested parties.

Qualifications And Education

This position requires at least one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level in the normal line of progression.
